name: West Virginia Eats
subtitle: Pepperoni Rolls, Dogs & Ramps
description:
West Virginia's restaurants, from a warm pepperoni roll in Fairmont to ramps in April.

West Virginia Eats is a free guide to eating in West Virginia: 11 pepperoni roll bakeries, 5 hot dog stands, 6 Italian kitchens, 4 places that cook ramps in season and 4 Appalachian tables we checked by hand, plus 3,339 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 282 towns, from Charleston and Morgantown to Huntington and Wheeling. No account, no ads.

WEST VIRGINIA GUIDES
• Pepperoni Rolls: bakeries on the Pepperoni Roll Trail, Fairmont to Clarksburg.
• West Virginia Hot Dogs: a dog with chili, slaw and onions.
• Italian Classics: the coal towns, Huntington and Wheeling.
• Ramps in Season: kitchens that cook wild ramps in spring.
• Appalachian Tables: Appalachian cooking from local farms.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "pepperoni roll", "hot dog slaw", "ramps".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 source or West Virginia Tourism's own listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists. West Virginia's local health departments publish no results as data, so each place links the state's food safety page. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the West Virginia Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of West Virginia or any West Virginia health department), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: West Virginia Eats is a free guide to restaurants in West Virginia (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: pepperoni rolls, hot dogs with chili and slaw, Italian classics, ramps in season and Appalachian tables, 30 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 3,339 restaurants, cafés and bars in 282 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Pepperoni Rolls (or West Virginia Hot Dogs, Italian Classics, Ramps in Season, Appalachian Tables, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the state's food safety page in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("pepperoni roll", "hot dog slaw", "ramps").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside West Virginia (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on West Virginia, and distance sorting still works from where you are.

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the West Virginia Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and official tourism listings.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/west-virginia-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers West Virginia; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.

Support: nick@eatsranked.com
